name: Pool of Tears
summary: In the eastern Swamp of Sorrows, the Pool of Tears surrounds a sunken temple. Frenzies patrol its murky waters, and troll ruins line its drowned banks.

sections.title: A Drowned Sanctuary
sections.body: Atal'ai trolls raised a great ziggurat to Hakkar the Soulflayer, their bloodthirsty god. Ysera, the Dragon Aspect, was horrified by the blasphemies within. She broke the ground beneath the temple and sank it into the marsh. Water covered the ruins, but the ziggurat still lies beneath silt and lake water. Green drakes keep watch nearby, guarding against the corruption sealed below.

sections.title: Waters of Peril
sections.body: Crossing the murky lake toward the sunken halls is perilous. Flesh-eating frenzies haunt the water, while Atal'ai artifacts and drowned stonework lie across the muddy floor. To reach the temple's upper passages, you must brave the hostile shallows. There, cultists and lingering dragon guardians struggle for control of the dark sanctuary.

faq.q: Why is it called the Pool of Tears?
faq.answer: No record tells why the lake is called the Pool of Tears. It is known for the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, which Ysera sank beneath its waters to stop Hakkar's summoning.

faq.q: What is the massive building in the center of the lake?
aliases: ruins in lake swamp of sorrows
faq.answer: The massive building in the lake is the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, often called the Sunken Temple. Once a towering Atal'ai ziggurat, it was sunk beneath the water by Ysera and remains partly submerged at the pool's center.

faq.q: Why are there green dragons around the water?
faq.answer: Ysera's brood came to destroy the temple and drown its vile ceremonies. Green drakes and dragonkin still watch the lake, keeping the Atal'ai cultists from completing their summoning of the Blood God.

faq.q: Is it safe to swim across the pool?
faq.answer: No. Aggressive, flesh-eating frenzies infest the lake and attack anyone swimming toward the temple entrance.

angles.text: As a Darkspear troll, you can see the pool as a grim warning of what follows when trollkind embraces forbidden blood magic like that of the Atal'ai.
As a druid, you can honor the lake as the place where Ysera and the Green Dragonflight intervened to stem the Blood God's taint.
